headline: High-risk filesystem and shell interaction: xonsh can overwrite Great Expectations inputs/results, creating default-path data corruption and leakage risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations reads and writes files for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while xonsh can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands. If xonsh feeds crafted file content into Great Expectations workflows, instruction-like text could be misread. The pathway is plausible in shared files, though not proven by direct interaction evidence.
conditions: IF xonsh writes attacker-controlled text into files later parsed by Great Expectations
IF Great Expectations consumes those files as trusted configuration or documentation
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Review file inputs before Great Expectations parses them
Use read-only mounts for Great Expectations inputs
Add a manual approval step for any generated config or docs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and xonsh can read filesystem contents and broad network egress. In a shared workspace, xonsh could read Great Expectations outputs and transmit them externally. This is not guaranteed, but the default filesystem access plus network egress makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable workspace
IF Great Expectations stores sensitive validation results in that workspace
IF xonsh is allowed to read those files and make outbound requests
mitigations: Store sensitive outputs outside the shared workspace
Restrict xonsh network egress
Use per-agent directories with strict permissions
Rotate or redact validation artifacts before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on filesystem reads and outbound requests

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation artifacts and documentation, and xonsh has unrestricted filesystem write plus shell/subprocess execution. Both can mutate the same directory, while xonsh also supports multiple command forms. With no locking or coordination shown, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite results in default shared-workspace setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory
IF Great Expectations writes validation outputs while xonsh writes or edits files there
IF no external lock or serialization is enforced
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize file writes with a lock file
Make Great Expectations outputs append-only
Run xonsh in a read-only workspace when possible
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that xonsh can read from the filesystem and act on via shell commands. If xonsh treats those outputs as authoritative, a bad validation artifact can cascade into incorrect commands or edits. The pair lacks any documented verification boundary, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes Great Expectations validation output without independent checks
IF that output is used to drive shell commands or file edits
mitigations: Require human review before acting on validation output
Validate output schema before use
Limit xonsh to read-only inspection of results
Keep generated reports separate from executable scripts
requires-engineering: add typed handoff contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations handles data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, while xonsh can access filesystem contents and broad network egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a generic compliance gap is visible: sensitive validation artifacts could be exposed if shared. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from its filesystem and egress behavior.
conditions: IF validation artifacts contain regulated or sensitive data
IF xonsh can read those artifacts and send them off-host
mitigations: Classify and label sensitive validation outputs
Restrict outbound network access for xonsh
Keep regulated data out of shared directories
Set short retention on validation artifacts
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement
